items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: So he was conductor of the Masbaum Orchestra

ctx.x: Now, where does the tuba come in?

The tuba came in when I went to Masbaum after Overbrook. And Masbaum was a school, Jules Masbaum was a philanthropist in Philadelphia who also promoted jazz music, like the Curtis family. That's why they named the school after him. And it was a vocational school but it was the first vocational school that had introduced music. And the director of that school, Jules Levine, was a graduate of Temple University, which had the college music, grade A thing in Philadelphia. So he was conductor of the Masbaum Orchestra…
And of course Masbaum, over the years has turned out a lot of well-known musicians.
